organizer: Avrupa Gençlik Parlamentosu Derneği — National Committee of the European Youth Parliament in Türkiye (international network under the Schwarzkopf Foundation Young Europe)
organizer_domain_provenance: PARTIAL — flagged. eyp.org.tr self-identifies as 'legally represented as the Avrupa Gençlik Parlamentosu Derneği since 2011' on its Who We Are page, which I fetched directly. Turkish .org.tr second-level domains are allocated by nic.tr against documentary proof of the applicant's legal entity name, so the domain string is itself weak corroboration of the association name. The international EYP site (eyp.org, run by the Schwarzkopf Foundation Young Europe) publicly features 'EYP Turkey' as a National Committee in its news section, which corroborates that the National Committee exists — but I fetched that page and it does NOT link to or name eyp.org.tr. So: the organisation is confirmed official within the EYP network, and the domain is strongly but not conclusively tied to it. An ingestion pipeline should either resolve the nic.tr WHOIS registrant or ask EYP international to confirm the domain before treating eyp.org.tr as an official domain.
city: Varies — sessions held in İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Mersin, Eskişehir, Alanya, Amasya, Çanakkale, Tarsus, Karadeniz Ereğli
program_dates: Next confirmed event: Mersin 2026, National Selection Conference, listed as '9 Kasım 2026' (9 November 2026). Recent completed events: Training Weekend 2026 (25 Temmuz 2026), İstanbul 2026 National Session (18 Temmuz 2026), Alanya 2026 RSC (22 Mayıs 2026), Eskişehir 2026 RSC (24 Nisan 2026), Amasya 2026 RSC (6 Şubat 2026).
duration: Individual sessions run a few days; national selection conferences feed delegates into the National Session and onward to International Sessions.
financial_aid: EYP network FAQ: 'If you are unable to pay the participation fee, but you still wish to participate, please reach out to the facilitators of the events to see how they can accommodate your needs.'
selection_process: Delegates apply per event; the network FAQ states 'To be selected as a participant, all you need to show is clear motivation and curiosity about EYP. We are not looking for experts or scientists, just young people eager to learn together.' Delegates selected at national selection conferences progress to the National Session and can be selected onward to International Sessions.
individual_or_team: individual applicant, committee-based teamwork at the event
award_or_output: Committee resolutions debated and voted in a simulated parliamentary General Assembly; progression to National Session and International Sessions; eligibility to take official roles (Chair, Organiser, Ambassador) after a first session.
latest_verified_cycle: 2026 — Mersin 2026 NSC listed as upcoming with 'Application link coming soon' when fetched on 2026-08-21
leadership_evidence: GENUINE, and unusually well-structured for this age band. The official Get Involved page describes four escalating pathways: Delegates (attend a session and debate), School Clubs (student/teacher ambassadors bring EYP into their school), Volunteers ('taking official roles after first session' — Chair, Organisers), and Alumni. The site posted 'Officer Calls are Now Open!' for 'academic and organizational' roles. A participant can therefore credibly demonstrate: selected as a delegate through a competitive national conference; co-authored and defended a committee resolution before a General Assembly; and, on progression, held a named appointed role (Chair of a committee, or Organiser of a multi-day national conference) — i.e. an actual, verifiable position of responsibility rather than attendance. The organisation is itself youth-run, which is what makes the officer roles real.

What is genuinely evidenced on the European Parliament's own page: students negotiate, amend, vote and adopt resolutions in the Strasbourg hemicycle, and the school reaches Euroscola by winning a national competition — so selection is real and the civic content is real. What is NOT evidenced: any sustained role, team ownership, or measurable outcome. It is a single day. A student can honestly claim 'selected as part of my school's delegation, through a national competition, to the European Parliament's Euroscola day' — a credible civic distinction — but not a leadership position. A counselor should file this under civic exposure and selection distinction, not leadership.

However, the How to participate page routes ALL selection through European Parliament Liaison Offices, which exist in Member States; I did not find a Liaison Office covering Türkiye, and I did not find any page confirming Turkish school participation. age_range.quote: at least 13 years old to learn and tutor on Schoolhouse.world

prerequisites: No prior teaching or tutoring experience required
Demonstrated subject knowledge via the certification process (not a degree or formal credential)
duration: Rolling and self-paced; no mandatory hour commitment is published. Sessions can be as short as a 30-minute group session.
financial_aid: n/a — free to both tutors and learners
selection_process: Choose a Khan Academy unit; score at least 90% on the unit test while video-recording yourself working and explaining your reasoning; peer-review two other candidates' submissions; then complete self-paced training modules on running a safe, effective session.
required_materials: Video recording of a Khan Academy unit test attempt with spoken reasoning
Peer reviews of two other candidates
award_or_output: Publicly shareable certification transcript showing mastery across topics; a portfolio of certifications and tutoring experience; sessions hosted and led by the tutor; college partners view the credential as a demonstration of academic achievement.
leadership_evidence: REAL BUT MODEST — and unusually verifiable, which is its actual value. The official page confirms certified tutors host and run their own group sessions after training, and that the platform issues a publicly shareable transcript and portfolio recording both certifications and tutoring experience. So a student can demonstrate: independently certified in named subjects at a 90% mastery bar; led N of their own tutoring sessions; and the claim is externally checkable at a public URL — rare for teenage service claims, which are usually unverifiable. What it is NOT: there is no team to manage, no elected role, and no published minimum commitment, so hours accrue only as much as the student chooses. For a counselor this is a low-barrier, high-verifiability way to build a documented service record; it is not a leadership position.
